About Tyler

About me

I'm pursuing a Bachelor of Science in Computer Engineering Technology at Farmingdale State College, with graduation expected in May 2027. I also work as an Embedded Engineering Intern at Stellant Systems in Melville, New York.

Based on Long Island, NY, my interests span embedded systems, electronics, and hands-on hardware work. Outside engineering, I draw, paint, travel, and take photos.

Background

Building and troubleshooting computers has been a long-running interest. Since 2018, I've built and configured more than 20 desktop systems, choosing components for performance, compatibility, and budget while working through hardware, software, and thermal issues.

My engineering work now includes microcontroller firmware, digital logic, and communication between devices. At Stellant Systems, I've worked on PIC32 & ARM firmware, power-supply telemetry, FPGA connectivity testing, and software interfaces for networked hardware.

For my senior design project, I'm leading a three-person team developing a wireless system to control, monitor, and independently verify multiple custom linear DC power supplies.

I also help organize technical workshops through Farmingdale's IEEE Student Branch. My Multi-Arduino Morse Code Telegraph project brings together serial communication, pushbutton input, and LCD output in a hands-on workshop.

Tools & experience

Technical skills

  • Programming: C, C++, VHDL, and Assembly.
  • Embedded systems: PIC and ARM microcontrollers, Arduino, and FPGA design.
  • Communications: UART, I2C, SPI, and TCP/IP.
  • Bench work: Oscilloscopes, multimeters, logic analyzers, electronic loads, soldering, and hardware troubleshooting.
  • Development tools: MPLAB IDE, NI LabWindows/CVI, NI Multisim, Proteus, Arduino IDE, Visual Studio, and Vivado.
  • PC hardware: Component selection, assembly, repair, and system optimization.
